name: Anisotropic Screen-Space Fluid Rendering
aliases: Anisotropic screen space rendering for particle-based fluid simulation
definition: A real-time fluid rendering method that applies anisotropic transformations to point sprites to stretch them along appropriate axes, obtaining smooth fluid surfaces based on the weighted principal components analysis (WPCA) of the particle distribution. It combines processed anisotropic point sprite information with screen space filters to resolve jagged edges and unevenness while preserving sharp high-frequency details.
summary: Anisotropic Screen-Space Fluid Rendering converts particle data into continuous fluid volumes using elliptical sprites to preserve sharp details and avoid the jagged edges of standard isotropic methods.
